synopsis: For road vehicles, the UNECE New Assessment/Test Method (NATM), documented in WP.29/2022/58 with guidelines WP.29/2023/44, places simulation within a multi-pillar validation approach alongside a scenario catalogue, track tests, real-world tests, audit and in-service monitoring [f1716, f9743]. The corpus identifies NATM's 2022 and 2023 work as a simulation credibility framework covering management, analysis, verification, validation and uncertainty [f7531, f9744]. The outcome of the credibility assessment defines the envelope in which a virtual tool can be used, rather than granting unrestricted use [f9745]. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1426 has an annex related to this virtual-testing credibility framework [f9747]. However, no study by the listed industry and standards bodies was found applying NATM, OpenSCENARIO or ISO 34502 to off-road machines, leaving an off-road application evidence gap [f1698].

relations.note: Adds document references, scenario catalogue and in-service monitoring to the shared multi-pillar approach.
Specifies the components of the simulation credibility framework.
Permitted virtual-tool use depends on the credibility assessment outcome.
Identifies a related EU regulatory annex for the virtual-testing credibility framework.
Qualifies the road-vehicle method with a gap in identified off-road application studies.
